newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers seek tough conditions on tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers seek tough conditions on tobacco deal.

text.p: A group of Democratic members of Congress called Wednesday for stringent conditions to be included in any settlement of litigation against the tobacco industry.

In a letter to President Bill Clinton, they said a settlement should subject the tobacco companies to wide-ranging regulation by the Federal Food and Drug Administration, a campaign against teen smoking and stepped up warnings on cigarette packs.

The lawmakers, led by Sen. Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Democrat, were reacting to news reports of negotiations between plaintiffs' lawyers and tobacco firms and of a possible settlement of $300 billion over 25 years.
The letter urged Clinton to "maintain a healthy scepticism" toward any proposed settlement and to insist on a set of requirements before the administration assented to an agreement.

"We are on the cusp of victory and should not allow the tobacco industry to use a global settlement to turn the tide against necessary protections to the public health, plaintiffs, our taxpayers and our children," the letter said.

At a news conference, Lautenberg, along with Sens Dick Durbin of Illinois and Paul Wellstone of Minnesota and Representative Martin Meehan of Massachusetts, said Congress would play a key role in any final settlement. "Ultimately Congress will be the final arbiter," Meehan said.
